_doc: OPERATOR presentation overlay (tax-treaty-navigator — Bee-D build 4e6f5c29-2977-4c42-9b7e-5045ed8c268a). The emitter merges the machine engine (content+routing) with this overlay -> engine.json (terminals schema). Bee-D never sets tier/severity — that separation is doctrine, and scripts/emit-engine.ts refuses to emit without this file. Dishes take heading from the menu label + result_copy from the grounded result_state unless overridden here; NEITHER is overridden in this draft, so every word a buyer reads is the machine's grounded copy. Escapes REQUIRE heading+result_copy in this file (translate-to-terminals defaults them to empty strings and validateTerminalsEngine then refuses on 'missing heading'/'missing result_copy'); tier is FORCED to 67 on every escape regardless of what this file says, so the escape entries below carry no tier key — matching spain-beckham-eligibility/presentation.json exactly.
_ruling:
DRAFT — every line below is a PROPOSAL. The operator rules each one.
SHAPE PRECEDENT: app/nomad/check/spain-beckham-eligibility/presentation.json (origin/main 33a7b10). Same three top-level keys (_doc/_ruling/states); dish entries carry {tier, severity, criticality, title_key}; escape entries carry {severity, criticality, title_key, heading, result_copy} and NO tier. No field is invented here.

TIER DOCTRINE APPLIED: standard/simple outcome = 67; structural complexity (multi-jurisdiction structuring, entity/agreement analysis, elections with procedural timing work) = 147; explainers, ongoing-guidance dishes, and ALL escape/disqualified states = 67.

PROPOSED 147 (2 of 8 dishes) — both are analysis ACROSS two tax authorities, not a lookup:
  ambiguous-treaty-language = 147/amber/critical. The dish is the interpretation of a bilateral AGREEMENT whose two signatories may read the same clause differently; its own grounded copy says the exposure is 'double taxation or unexpected liability' and that 'this menu cannot resolve ambiguous treaty language for specific facts'. That is agreement analysis across jurisdictions, which the doctrine puts at 147.
  permanent-establishment = 147/amber/critical. ENTITY/presence analysis — fixed place of business, an agent with authority to conclude contracts, duration of activities — followed by profit attribution under the business-profits article. Structural on both limbs, and the outcome decides whether a business is taxable in the host country at all.

PROPOSED 67 — explainers and ongoing guidance:
  what-treaties-are = 67/amber/standard. Pure explainer; asserts no outcome about the reader. Seeded from the beckham explainer precedent (regime-duration-explainer, tax-rates-explainer: both 67/amber/standard).
  treaty-article-outcomes = 67/amber/standard. A lookup — which article governs which income type. The work is reading the right article, not structuring anything.
  claiming-withholding-relief = 67/amber/standard. Procedural and named: give the withholding agent a W-8BEN or W-8BEN-E. CLOSEST CALL #2 — the doctrine sends 'elections with procedural timing work' to 147, and a treaty claim is an election of sorts. Proposed 67 because it carries no statutory deadline and no structuring: the form is filed with a counterparty, not an authority, and the failure mode (default statutory withholding) is recoverable rather than permanent. Flip to 147 if Strategy reads the W-8 route as election work.
  treaty-documentation = 67/amber/standard. Ongoing guidance — what to establish and retain. Mentions limitation-on-benefits, but as a record-keeping requirement, not an analysis to perform.
  escape-professional = 67/amber/standard. A MENU dish whose whole content is a referral to an international tax professional; the doctrine puts every disqualified/referral state at 67. NOTE FOR THE OPERATOR: this dish will additionally render ESCAPE-CLASS at runtime without any overlay help — engine-terms.isQuasiEscape treats a menu dish with zero resolvable figures and referral-only copy as an escape, and this build's figure pool is EMPTY (0 figures), so its copy ('general guidance cannot reliably address') trips the referral cue with no numeric token to disqualify it. Tier 67 is therefore the only self-consistent value.

CLOSEST CALL #1 — treaty-domestic-interaction = 67/amber/critical, and it is the one row most likely to be flipped. It is the ONLY terminal reachable from two different questions with different intent: q1 'I want to understand how treaty rules interact with US domestic tax law' (explainer-shaped) and q3 'How the treaty rule (including any PE determination) interacts with US domestic tax law' (a live business question downstream of a PE fact pattern). Tier is per-TERMINAL, not per-path, so one number has to serve both. Proposed 67 because the dish's own label and the bulk of its grounded copy are explanatory, and because pricing an explainer path at 147 is the dish_class_mislabel the AI-review gate hard-fails. Criticality is critical rather than standard because the copy is explicit that a treaty provision may override or modify a domestic rule and that 'professional review of the interaction in your specific situation is indicated' — real exposure, mirroring beckham's loss-of-status-guidance (67 + critical). If Strategy prefers the q3 reading to dominate, 147/amber/critical is the defensible alternative and the only change needed is this one number.

SEVERITY: no dish in this build asserts a positive eligibility outcome, so nothing takes beckham's green (which it used only for its clean qualifying route); and nothing here is a definite exclusion, so nothing takes red. Every dish is amber — a real position that still depends on the specific treaty and facts. none_fit takes blue per precedent.

ESCAPES: heading + result_copy are authored here because the engine has no content for escape states and the validator refuses an empty one. Written to orient, not to sell — each says what is unresolved and what would resolve it, and none promises an outcome.

PROVENANCE: build_jobs 4e6f5c29-2977-4c42-9b7e-5045ed8c268a, build_state GATES_PASSED, product nomad/check/tax-treaty-navigator (taxchecknow). research_output.calculator: 8 menu dishes + 3 escape_states + 3 questions, provenance_mode independent_voice, grounded in the IRS United States income tax treaties authority. Figure pool: 0 figures, so every terminal emits figure_ids: [].

none_fit.heading: A tax treaty may not be what your question turns on
none_fit.result_copy: US income tax treaties allocate taxing rights between the United States and one other country, for a defined list of income types, and only for people and entities that are residents of one of the two countries. A question that does not sit inside that frame — a purely domestic US filing question, an immigration or visa question, a question about a country with no US treaty in force, or a state-level tax question, since states are generally not bound by federal treaties — will not be answered by reading a treaty, and that is worth knowing early rather than after the reading. The useful next step is to identify which body of law your question actually belongs to and take it to someone who works in that area: a US domestic tax preparer, the relevant state revenue authority, or an immigration adviser, as the case may be.

insufficient_information.heading: Your treaty question needs one more detail before it can be answered
insufficient_information.result_copy: Your answers do not yet identify which treaty question you are actually asking, and the answer changes completely depending on which it is. A treaty analysis needs three things before it can start: the treaty country, because reduced rates and exemptions vary between treaties and no general answer holds across them; the income type, because a separate article governs dividends, interest, royalties, capital gains, employment income and business profits, and they do not agree with one another; and your residence status for treaty purposes, which turns on residence rather than citizenship. Once those three are settled the applicable article is usually identifiable from the treaty text and the IRS technical explanation for it. If they are not settled, an international tax adviser can establish them from your facts faster than a general menu can.

high_complexity.heading: Your situation has two moving parts that interact
high_complexity.result_copy: You have indicated a situation with more than one live treaty issue at the same time — a benefit claim together with its documentation basis, or a permanent-establishment question together with how the treaty rule meets US domestic law. These do not decompose cleanly: how a benefit is claimed depends on what can be evidenced, and what a permanent-establishment finding means in practice depends on the domestic rule it lands against. Answering either half on its own can produce advice that the other half contradicts, which is why this menu stops here rather than picking one. An international tax professional can hold both parts together, assess the applicable treaty and article, and check any limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse provision that bears on the combination.
